subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A trapdoor (uniform, weight 50 N, width 1.2 m) is hinged along one edge and held horizontal by a vertical rope at the opposite edge. The rope tension is:
questions.explain: Moments about the hinge: T x 1.2 = 50 x 0.6, so T = 25 N.

questions.q: A force of 10 N acts at 30 degrees to a rod at a point 2 m from a pivot. What is the moment about the pivot?
questions.explain: Moment = 10 x 2 x sin30 = 10 x 2 x 0.5 = 10 Nm.

questions.q: A uniform rod rests on two supports. As a load is moved toward one support, the rod is on the point of tilting about that support when which condition holds?
options: The reaction at the near support is zero
The reaction at the other support is zero
questions.explain: At the point of tilting about a support, the far support is about to lift off, so its reaction is zero.

questions.q: Forces act on a lever pivoted at O: 5 N at 0.6 m clockwise, 3 N at 0.4 m clockwise, and 9 N at distance d anticlockwise. For equilibrium, d is closest to:
questions.explain: Clockwise = 5 x 0.6 + 3 x 0.4 = 4.2; 9 x d = 4.2 gives d = 0.467 m.

questions.q: A uniform beam AB of length 6 m and weight 60 N rests on supports at A and B. What is the reaction at A?
questions.explain: By symmetry the uniform weight splits equally, so each reaction is 60/2 = 30 N.

questions.q: A uniform ladder of weight W and length L leans against a smooth wall at angle theta to the horizontal. The wall reaction is S. Taking moments about the base, which equation is correct?
options: S x L cos theta = W x (L/2) sin theta
S x L sin theta = W x (L/2) cos theta
S x L = W x L/2
questions.explain: The wall reaction acts horizontally at height L sin theta; the weight acts at horizontal distance (L/2) cos theta from the base.

questions.q: A ladder rests against a smooth wall and on rough ground. Which force is absent at the wall?
questions.explain: A smooth wall exerts no friction, so only a normal reaction acts there.

questions.q: A 2 m uniform rod of weight 30 N hangs from two vertical strings at its ends with a 60 N weight 0.5 m from the left end. The tension in the right string is:
questions.explain: Total downward load = 90 N, so T_R = 90 - 60 = 30 N.

questions.q: A uniform rod of length 2L and weight W is pivoted at distance L/2 from one end. A weight P hung at that near end balances it. Find P.
questions.explain: The centre of mass is at L, i.e. L/2 from the pivot; the near end is L/2 on the other side: P x (L/2) = W x (L/2), so P = W.

questions.q: A 2 m uniform rod of weight 30 N hangs from two vertical strings at its ends. A 60 N weight is placed 0.5 m from the left end. The tension in the left string is:
questions.explain: Moments about the right end: T_L x 2 = 30 x 1 + 60 x 1.5 = 120, so T_L = 60 N.

questions.q: A uniform rod of weight 80 N and length 6 m has its centre at 3 m and rests on supports at 1 m and 4 m from end A. A weight W hangs at end A and the rod is about to tilt about the 1 m support. Find W.
questions.explain: At tilt the 4 m reaction is 0; moments about the 1 m support: W x 1 = 80 x 2 (centre is 2 m from the support), so W = 160 N.

questions.q: A uniform rod rests on supports P and Q. The system is on the point of tilting about Q. At this instant the reaction at P is:
questions.explain: On the point of tilting about Q, support P is about to lift off, so its reaction is zero.

questions.q: Two forces, 8 N (clockwise, 2 m) and an unknown F (anticlockwise, 4 m), act on a pivoted rod in equilibrium. Find F.
questions.explain: For equilibrium clockwise = anticlockwise: 8 x 2 = F x 4, so F = 4 N.

questions.q: A uniform ladder on rough ground leans against a smooth wall in limiting equilibrium. Resolving horizontally gives which relationship between friction F and wall reaction S?
questions.explain: The only horizontal forces are friction at the base and the wall reaction, so F = S.

questions.q: A uniform rod of weight 40 N and length 2 m rests on a pivot 0.5 m from its left end. What downward force at the left end keeps it horizontal?
questions.explain: Centre of mass is 1 m from the left, i.e. 0.5 m right of the pivot: F x 0.5 = 40 x 0.5, so F = 40 N.

questions.q: A uniform plank of weight 100 N and length 4 m rests on supports at its ends with a 200 N load 1 m from the left support. What is the reaction at the right support?
questions.explain: Total load is 300 N, so the right reaction = 300 - 200 = 100 N.

questions.q: A non-uniform rod AB of length 4 m and weight 50 N balances on a single pivot 1.5 m from A. Where is its centre of mass?
questions.explain: A rod balances on a single pivot only when its centre of mass is directly above it, i.e. 1.5 m from A.

questions.q: A uniform beam of weight 600 N and length 8 m is supported at points 2 m and 6 m from end A. By symmetry, what is the reaction at each support?
questions.explain: The supports are symmetric about the centre, so each carries half the weight: 600/2 = 300 N.

questions.q: A uniform rod AB of weight 40 N and length 4 m rests on a pivot at its midpoint. A 10 N weight hangs 1 m from the pivot on one side. A weight hung 2 m from the pivot on the other side balances it. What weight is needed?
questions.explain: Balancing moments about the pivot: 10 x 1 = W x 2, so W = 5 N.

questions.q: A uniform plank of weight 100 N and length 4 m rests on supports at its two ends. A 200 N load sits 1 m from the left support. What is the reaction at the left support?
questions.explain: Moments about the right support: R_L x 4 = 100 x 2 + 200 x 3 = 800, so R_L = 200 N.

questions.q: A light rod AB of length 5 m has a 30 N weight 1 m from A and is supported at A and B. What is the reaction at A?
questions.explain: Total reaction equals the weight: R_A = 30 - 6 = 24 N.

questions.q: A light rod AB of length 5 m has a 30 N weight 1 m from A and is supported at A and B. What is the reaction at B?
questions.explain: Taking moments about A: R_B x 5 = 30 x 1, so R_B = 6 N.

questions.q: A horizontal rod of weight 12 N and length 0.4 m is hinged at a wall and held by a vertical wire at its outer end. What is the wire tension?
questions.explain: Moments about the hinge: T x 0.4 = 12 x 0.2, so T = 6 N.

questions.q: A horizontal force of 50 N is applied to the rim of a wheel of radius 0.3 m. The moment about the axle is:
questions.explain: Moment = 50 x 0.3 = 15 Nm.

questions.q: A see-saw is balanced when a child of weight 300 N sits 1.5 m from the pivot. How far from the pivot must a 450 N child sit on the other side?
A signpost is a uniform horizontal rod of weight 40 N and length 1 m fixed at a wall. The turning moment it exerts about the wall fixing equals:
questions.explain: The weight acts at the centre, 0.5 m out: moment = 40 x 0.5 = 20 Nm.

questions.q: A uniform rod of length 3 m and mass 5 kg is supported horizontally at one end and held by a vertical force at the other. Take g = 9.8. What is that force?
questions.explain: Weight 5 x 9.8 = 49 N acts at the centre (1.5 m); moments about the supported end: F x 3 = 49 x 1.5, so F = 24.5 N.

questions.q: A force of 12 N acts perpendicular to a rod at a point 0.5 m from a pivot. What is the moment of the force about the pivot?
questions.explain: Moment = force x perpendicular distance = 12 x 0.5 = 6 Nm.

questions.q: A uniform rod of length 4 m and weight 20 N rests horizontally on a single support at its centre. What is the reaction at the support?
questions.explain: The single support carries the whole weight, so the reaction equals 20 N.

questions.q: A non-uniform plank AB of length 5 m and weight 200 N rests on supports at A and B. The reaction at A is 120 N. How far from A is the centre of mass?
questions.explain: Moments about B: R_A x 5 = 200 x (5 - x), so 600 = 1000 - 200x, giving x = 2.0 m.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel Level 3 Advanced GCE in Mathematics (9MA0) specification; Moments
